result.title: DiffNash: Finding Nash Equilibrium in High-Dimensional Continuous Action Spaces with Diffusion Policies
result.summary: Computing equilibria in high-dimensional continuous games requires learning and representing rich, multi-modal strategy distributions, something conventional neural policies struggle to achieve. Diffusion models offer a natural solution, but standard diffusion training requires direct samples from a fixed target distribution, which are generally unavailable under iterative game-solving updates. We propose a diffusion-based framework for equilibrium computation that enables diffusion-based variants of Online Mirror Descent (OMD) and Fictitious Play (FP). Our approach derives a reweighted score-matching objective that trains diffusion policies without requiring direct samples from each updated policy. Our main method, DiffNash, combines the fast convergence of OMD with the sample efficiency of FP by reusing past actions through a replay buffer. To correct the resulting distribution shift from sample reuse, we derive an unbiased estimator of the difference between current and past policies' Evidence Lower Bounds, whose exponential provides a tractable proxy for the corresponding importance weight without evaluating diffusion likelihoods. We evaluate our approach on forest protection games and continuous Colonel Blotto games, reducing the Nash gap over the strongest baseline by 35.6% and 24.7%, respectively, with minimal hyperparameter tuning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 DiffNash，用扩散策略在高维连续动作空间中求解 Nash 均衡：推导重加权 score matching 目标，使扩散策略无需来自更新后目标分布的样本即可训练，并用当前与历史策略 ELBO 之差的无偏估计作为重要性权重代理，结合 OMD 与 FP 及 replay buffer，在森林保护与连续 Colonel Blotto 博弈上降低 Nash gap。
AI.relevance_reason: 迭代求解中目标策略分布持续漂移、无法直接采样的问题，与 LVR 中 latent 推理状态的分布训练、轨迹监督和贡献分配有一定结构相似性；其「无似然的重加权/重要性权重估计」可能为 latent 状态训练中的分布偏移校正提供可核查线索。
